title: Paid-Up Seasonal Storage Terms in the Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements Catalogue
content:
One programme in the Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements catalogue sells storage up front for a season rather than billing it period by period, and this note records the rate and the date it runs through across the catalogue.

## Basis of the charge

Paid-up storage is bought at a single up-front rate for each bushel signed in, and that payment carries the grain through the month and day posted for the programme. Where a programme offers no paid-up storage, no flat rate stands against it and no paid-up date is posted.

## Posted paid-up terms

| Programme | Paid-up rate (USD per bushel) | Paid-up storage runs through |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open Storage Account | 0.0000 | not offered |
| Grain Bank Deposit Account | 0.0000 | not offered |
| Commercial Warehouse Receipt Storage | 0.0000 | not offered |
| Seasonal Paid-Up Storage Agreement | 0.2200 | 09-01, the first day of September |
| Conditioned Reserve Storage Agreement | 0.0000 | not offered |
| Identity Preserved Segregated Storage | 0.0000 | not offered |

## Same terms, put as a question and answer

**What does a member on the Seasonal Paid-Up Storage Agreement pay, and for how long?** Twenty-two hundredths of a dollar for each bushel signed in, which is the posted rate of 0.2200 per bushel, and that payment carries those bushels through the first day of September.

**What does a nil rate against the other five programmes mean?** That the programme does not sell storage up front at all; its storage is quoted period by period rather than as a flat rate through a posted date.

## Worked illustration, on a hypothetical quantity

A member signing 12000 bushels of corn into a Seasonal Paid-Up Storage Agreement buys storage through the first day of September at 0.2200 for each bushel: twelve thousand multiplied by twenty-two hundredths of a dollar, which is 2640.00 in total.
